title: When deaths go uncounted: WHO flags dangerous blind spots in Africa’s health data
keyFacts: Quality health data can help authorities to identify emerging threats and take lifesaving action, but a new report reveals critical gaps in Africa’s health information systems.

title: Sudan war: First suicide bombers, now long-range drone strikes are the norm
keyFacts: Drones and drought are “closing in” on Sudan, the UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF), said on Tuesday, describing unprecedented attacks on the country’s infrastructure including by drones travelling up to 1,500 kilometres before hitting their target.

title: Climate crisis could push 141 million more women into extreme poverty
keyFacts: More than one in three women and girls worldwide – roughly 1.5 billion – live in so-called “climate hotspots”, where high exposure to hazards such as cyclones and droughts combine with insecure jobs and deep gender inequality.

title: World News in Brief: El Niño’s $11 trillion price tag, Mozambique and Yemen updates
keyFacts: The El Niño extreme weather pattern could cost the global economy up to $11 trillion and seriously impact food security, said the UN agency tackling rural poverty in developing countries on Monday.

title: Children among the dead as heavy rains flood tents and shelters in Gaza
keyFacts: An infant reportedly drowned and five Gazans were killed – including three children – when a sand dune collapsed on their tents as the first heavy rains swept across the enclave at the weekend, according to the UN aid coordination office (OCHA).

title: Families who fled Ethiopia for Kenya’s Moyale need food, water and shelter
keyFacts: The International Organization of Migration (IOM) and partners are calling for urgent funding to support tens of thousands of people who have escaped violent clashes in Ethiopia for the Moyale region in northern Kenya.
